content:
Field
Description
ContextTimeStamp
System time of event creation.
EventTapId
The macOS assigned identifier of the Event Tap.
EventTapPoint
Describes the point in macOS where the events are captured.
Values:
HID_EVENT_TAP (0)
SESSION_EVENT_TAP (1)
ANNOTATED_SESSION_EVENT_TAP (2)
EventTapOptions
Indicates if the macOS Event Tap is an active filter or passive listener.
Values:
ACTIVE_FILTER (0)
PASSIVE_LISTENER (1)
EventTapEventsOfInterest
Indicates which macOS HID events are being captured.
Values:
NULL_EVENT (1)
LEFT_MOUSE_BUTTON_DOWN_EVENT (2)
LEFT_MOUSE_BUTTON_UP_EVENT (4)
RIGHT_MOUSE_BUTTON_DOWN_EVENT (8)
RIGHT_MOUSE_BUTTON_UP_EVENT (16)
MOUSE_MOVED_EVENT (32)
LEFT_MOUSE_BUTTON_DRAGGED_EVENT (64)
RIGHT_MOUSE_BUTTON_DRAGGED_EVENT (128)
KEY_DOWN_EVENT (1024)
KEY_UP_EVENT (2048)
FLAGS_CHANGED_EVENT (4096)
SCROLL_WHEEL_EVENT (4194304)
TABLET_POINTER_EVENT (8388608)
TABLET_PROXIMITY_EVENT (16777216)
OTHER_MOUSE_BUTTON_DOWN_EVENT (33554432)
OTHER_MOUSE_BUTTON_UP_EVENT (67108864)
OTHER_MOUSE_BUTTON_DRAGGED_EVENT (134217728)
SourceProcessId
UPID of creating process.
Note that in Windows [http://msdn.microsoft.com/en- us/library/windows/hardware/ff559960%28v=vs.85%29.aspx] , the
ParentProcessId does not have to be the same as SourceProcessId since a different parent can be specified for creation. On
Mac, SourceProcessId is the responsible_pid which is used by XPC to note the process requesting this XPC process.
TargetProcessId
The unique ID of a target process (in decimal, non-hex format). This field exists in almost all events, and it represents the ID of the
process that is responsible for the activity of the event in focus. For example, the TargetProcessId of a process that performed
thread injection in an InjectedThread event
EventTapIsEnabled
Indicates if the macOS Event Tap is enabled.
